Query: why did Shipyard evict all the pods on node wk-17? disk usage was only around 80% on /

Retrieved: Shipyard Orchestrator Operations Guide, chapter 7 'Node pressure and eviction'

7.1 Overview. Each node agent monitors memory, disk and process-ID availability. When a resource drops below a configured threshold, the node is marked as under pressure and the scheduler stops placing new workloads there. If pressure persists, the node agent begins evicting workloads to reclaim the resource.

7.2 Disk signals. Two disk signals are tracked separately: nodefs, the filesystem holding the node agent's data and container logs, and imagefs, the filesystem holding container images and writable layers. On many installations these are different mount points, so the root filesystem can look healthy while imagefs is full. The default hard eviction threshold is 10% free space on either filesystem, and 5% free inodes on nodefs.

7.3 Eviction order. Workloads are ranked by priority class and then by how far their usage exceeds their requests. Best-effort workloads with no requests set are evicted first. Critical system workloads are never evicted by the node agent.

7.4 Soft thresholds. Operators can configure soft thresholds with a grace period; the agent waits for the grace period before evicting. Soft thresholds are disabled by default.

7.5 Changing thresholds. Thresholds are set in the node agent configuration file under evictionHard and evictionSoft. Changes take effect after the agent restarts.

7.6 Logging. Eviction events are recorded with reason DiskPressure, MemoryPressure or PIDPressure and can be viewed with `shipctl events --node <name>`.

7.7 Related reading. See chapter 9 for sizing guidance and chapter 12 for log rotation.
